A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, Generalizable Neural Electromagnetic Inverse Scattering. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–C are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction experiments on Circular, MNIST, Institut Fresnel, and 3D MNIST, including baseline comparisons, ablations, and repeated-trial statistics.

after.justification: v3 retains original reconstruction experiments and adds qualitative single-transmitter results on 3D ShapeNet in Section 5.4 and Appendix C.2.

M1.justification: The current estimator, physics-based permittivity solver, transmitter-specific solver pairs, averaging fusion, and three training losses remain unchanged. The 3D extension already exists in v1; applying it to ShapeNet introduces no documented procedural change.

E1.justification: v3 adds training and evaluation on 3D ShapeNet, substantively expanding the 3D object population beyond handwritten digits to varied geometries including airplanes, cars, sofas, and tables. Section 5.4 and Appendix C.2 demonstrate this new coverage; all four earlier datasets remain.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the retained experiments: BP, 2-fold SOM, Gs SOM, BPS, PGAN, Physics-Net, and Img-Interiors retain their respective comparisons. The 3D MNIST comparison still uses Img-Interiors; the new ShapeNet figures show only the proposed method and ground truth.

E3.justification: The added ShapeNet experiment introduces 5,000 training samples from five categories and 500 test samples, with single-transmitter reconstruction reported in Figures 7 and 18. Existing datasets' splits, metrics, noise conditions, and training settings are unchanged; the new experiment follows the existing 3D acquisition setup.

E4.justification: Table 3 drops the Circular transmitter sweep, removing its intermediate N = 4, 8, and 12 results, while Table 4 drops quantitative loss ablations for two IF cases. One high-noise example also disappears from Figure 6. The MNIST ablations, noise comparisons, and appendix qualitative loss ablations remain, so the analytical questions are retained with narrower evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions' Appendix C.1 describes three independent Gaussian-noise trials and reports means and standard deviations in Table 5. The reporting practice and table values are unchanged; v3 introduces no additional uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: v3 adds qualitative ShapeNet reconstructions in Figures 7 and 18 but no ShapeNet numerical scores. Circular results at N = 4, 8, and 12, the IF loss-ablation metrics, and the digit-zero example in Figure 6 are removed. Matched numerical entries in Tables 2–5 remain unchanged, so there is no reported same-setting performance improvement.

T1.justification: The transmission–scattering reformulation, induced-current properties, equations, and Appendix A physical model remain unchanged. No mathematical assumption, derivation, definition, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about a generalizable physics-driven framework, fast feed-forward reconstruction, sparse-transmitter robustness, and 3D applicability. ShapeNet supplies additional evidence without redefining those core claims.

C2.justification: Section 5.4 and Appendix C.2 newly interpret reconstruction of complex ShapeNet structures as evidence of broader geometric generalization and practical applicability. Earlier mechanism explanations and the explicit limitation concerning unexplored transmitter placement remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix B.1 documents ShapeNet sample counts and explicitly applies the shared 3D synthesis parameters to it, including permittivity 2, 400 MHz frequency, a 2-metre cubic region, and 160 receivers. Existing architecture, optimizer, loss weights, hardware, and project-access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds Wu et al.'s 2015 3D ShapeNets reference for the new dataset. The related-work discussion and positioning against earlier inverse-scattering methods remain unchanged; other citation differences are renumbering.

P1.justification: v3 adds Section 5.4, short dataset and appendix passages, and clarifies that existing 3D figure captions concern MNIST. The introduction, method exposition, related work, and conclusion are otherwise substantially verbatim, without broad narrative restructuring.

P2.justification: Two ShapeNet figures are added, Figure 6 is shortened from three examples to two, and Tables 3 and 4 lose dataset columns and move into a side-by-side layout. Existing appendix figures are renumbered or relocated. These are localized display changes rather than a comprehensive visual redesign.

improvement.justification: ShapeNet adds useful evidence on more complex 3D objects, but its results are qualitative and provide no baseline comparison or numerical evaluation. Meanwhile, v3 removes Circular transmitter-sensitivity results and quantitative IF loss ablations rather than relocating them. Section 5.3 still cites Table 4 for IF metrics although that table now contains only MNIST. Broader geometric coverage therefore comes with weaker cross-dataset validation and a documentation inconsistency, leaving the net quality direction unclear.
